findings.title: Dogs treats a remote row containing one invalid item as absent and overwrites the whole account row with the local copy

scripts/test-data-safety-browser.cjs: malformed-row and rejected-initial-read cases (browser worker runs).
findings.rationale: Present malformed rows and absent rows returned the same null; successful reads then wrote all surfaces. Checked-in SQL permits inner malformed item schema, though current browser writer cannot generate that fixture. findings.title: Movies sync status is one global flag reset by any later success; partial failures (including Restore) report success
findings.rationale: Global success flag and swallowed results overstated durability. Each ranking/queue/pack row has pending/error/conflict state; restore distinguishes device-save outcome from remote sync. Unknown outcomes use CAS readback.

findings.title: Movies account writes are not serialized; reversed completion leaves an older list in the account
findings.rationale: Concurrent ordinary full-row saves can commit out of order. Browser request response delay alone is not proof of reversed DB commit, but audit gate correctly delayed mock commit itself; CAS and serialized read/write operations now prevent stale commits.
findings.reviewStatus: independent-adjudication-complete; final combined local verification passed

findings.title: A Dogs write that never completes stalls all later syncs while the UI says the ranking is backed up
verification: scripts/test-data-safety-browser.cjs: real 10-second hung-write timeout, later edit and reload.
findings.rationale: Thirty-second held-write evidence supports stalled queue and false backup status, not infinite network behavior. Sync now has bounded reads, conditional versioned writes with bounded readback, truthful pending/error/conflict states and retry. Late commits cannot overwrite a newer conditional version in updated clients.
findings.reviewStatus: independent-adjudication-complete; final combined local verification passed
limitations: Abort is not server rollback; legacy clients still need rollout handling.

findings.title: Backup fidelity edges: Dogs exports no pack progress if any entry has an unknown key; Movies drops out-of-range years, long titles and non-allowlisted fields
findings.rationale: Movies backup documentation expressly validates years and permits known fields only. Reject proposal to blindly preserve arbitrary fields; synthetic1865/320-character title do not establish ordinary valid-catalog data loss. Nevertheless identity-changing normalization was silent, so restore now explicitly warns before confirmation about title truncation, unsupported years and invalid entries. Dogs component separately adjudicated. Unknown progress fields are accepted by remote state/SQL but former strict exporter discarded all entries. Export now normalizes independently, keeps supported fields/entries, and includes explicit warning counts plus visible download warning. Strict restore validation is unchanged.
findings.reviewStatus: independent-adjudication-complete; final combined local verification passed
limitations: Unknown fields/invalid entries are omitted with explicit warning, not silently retained as trusted app state.

findings.title: Movies size pre-check accepts payloads the database CHECK rejects (JSON.stringify vs jsonb::text bytes)
auditEvidence: evidence/probes/helpers.json (moviesPayloadLimitMismatch, dogsPayloadAtFullCatalog: Dogs far below limit)
findings.rationale: Actual PostgreSQL 17.11 confirms compact JSON accepts payloads jsonb::text rejects. 3500 Movies: 1,010,391 compact versus 1,087,390 database bytes; 115 Dogs progress entries: 7,711 versus 8,285. New separate PostgreSQL byte estimator accounts for separators, UTF-8 and expanded numeric exponents; wire/backup measures remain exact and separate.
